To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a method that predicts the severity of cerebral ischaemia in gerbils before and after occlusion of a carotid artery by observing the diameter, appearance, and reactivity of the artery before and after temporary occlusion, and the severity of neurologic symptoms and signs after permanent occluion.
the severity of cerebral damage can be predicted by measuring the diameter and appearance after temporary occlusion of a carotid artery and observing clinical signs following permanent occlusions.

the severity of cerebral damage after permanent occlusion of the carotid artery can be predicted by the degree of arterial narrowing after temporary occlusion, and by clinical signs observed within 10 minutes after permanent occlusion, and that this prediction method is useful to investigate early ischemia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prediction of cerebral ischemia in the gerbil.
the development of a method for predicting the severity of cerebral infarction in the gerbil model of stroke.
the development of methods for predicting the severity of cerebral infarction and the evaluation of the effects of pharmacological agents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the method developed in this study to predict the severity and extent of cerebral ischemia is useful for studying the early stages of cerebral ischemia and is useful for evaluating the effectiveness in reducing the extent of ischemia of pharmacologic agents.

this prediction method can be used for the investigation of early cerebral ischemia in gerbils and for the evaluation of the effectiveness of pharmacological agents in reducing ischemic damage in this model.

the prediction method described is a reliable method to identify gerbils with severe ischemic damage and to predict the severity and the location of the damage before and after permanent occlusion of the carotid artery.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a simple, reliable, and rapid method to identify gerbils that would develop severe neurologic deficits after permanent occlusion of the left common carotid.
the gerbil model of permanent common carotid occlusion is useful to investigate early cerebral ischemia.

the severity of cerebral infarction can be predicted before permanent occlusion by the degree of reduction of arterial diameter and the appearance of the artery, and by the clinical signs of ischemia after permanent occlusion in gerbils.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the severity of cerebral injury is directly proportional to the severity of ischemia.

it is possible to predict the severity and location of ischemic brain injury before permanent carotid occlusion by observing clinical signs and the arterial diameter during and after temporary occlusion.
the method of prediction can be applied to any animal model of cerebral ischemia.
